# KRN-001: IPv4 forwarding is on where Docker runs

- **Group:** Kernel settings
- **Severity when it fails:** high
- **Root:** not needed

## Why it matters

Docker needs net.ipv4.ip_forward=1 to route container traffic. A hardening profile that sets it to 0 silently breaks container networking, and the failure looks like an application problem.

## Verify by hand

```sh
sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward; grep -r ip_forward /etc/sysctl.conf /etc/sysctl.d
```

## How to fix it

Set net.ipv4.ip_forward=1 in a sysctl drop-in and never let a hardening profile own it.

## What a fix can break

Turning forwarding on also lets the host route packets between interfaces; the firewall FORWARD policy then decides what passes.

Run `stackward explain KRN-001` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
